subtopic: Introductory
title: Essay response
action: Respond to something you have read in an extended written statement.
check: Did my statement deal with the text at length rather than in a phrase?

subtopic: Introductory
title: Pick the main idea
action: From a series of statements, choose the one that best expresses the main idea or ideas of the passage.
check: Does my choice express the passage's main idea, not just a detail?

subtopic: Introductory
title: Valid detail interpretation
action: From several statements about a detail, choose the only valid (or most apt) interpretation of the text.
check: Is my choice supported by the text better than the alternatives?

subtopic: Introductory
title: Spot the incorrect choice
action: From several statements about a detail, pick the one incorrect choice when the others are correct.
check: Can I show from the text why the chosen statement is wrong?

subtopic: Introductory
title: Recall a verbatim quotation
action: Recognise a verbatim quotation from the text to show you noticed and remembered it.
check: Do I remember where and in what words this appeared?

subtopic: Introductory
title: Fill the blank
action: Choose from a lettered list the phrase that, inserted in the blank, best completes the statement.
check: Does the completed statement make sense and match the text?

subtopic: Introductory
title: Bring outside knowledge
action: Answer using material outside the text that you are assumed to know already.
check: What did I know beforehand that the text does not say?

subtopic: Introductory
title: Draw valid inferences
action: Select the inferences that can reasonably be drawn from the text, and discard spurious ones with no foundation in it.
check: Is each inference I accept grounded in the text?

subtopic: Introductory
title: Reflect, not only score
action: Treat the questions as prompts to reflect on what you read; try the difficult ones, they may be most fun.
check: Did I think about why an answer is right, not just whether I scored?

subtopic: I. Exercises and Tests at the First Level of Reading: Elementary Reading
title: Read at comfortable speed
action: Read the short passage at a comfortable speed, about six to ten minutes for 1,200 words; speed is not essential.
check: Did I read steadily without rushing?

subtopic: I. Exercises and Tests at the First Level of Reading: Elementary Reading
title: Mark and note
action: Mark phrases and sentences that especially interest you and make a few notes before answering the questions.
check: Have I marked the striking passages and jotted notes?

subtopic: I. Exercises and Tests at the First Level of Reading: Elementary Reading
title: Adjust time to length
action: Allow more time for a longer text (ten to twelve minutes), again marking striking passages and making notes.
check: Did I scale my reading time to the passage length?

subtopic: I. Exercises and Tests at the First Level of Reading: Elementary Reading
title: Select all valid answers
action: Select every answer that seems valid, whether stated, implied, or true by logic or your background knowledge.
check: Have I considered implied and background-supported answers, not only stated ones?

subtopic: I. Exercises and Tests at the First Level of Reading: Elementary Reading
title: Historical context question
action: Answer a question about the historical setting of the subject's life that the passage does not state.
check: What do I know about the period that the text assumes?

subtopic: I. Exercises and Tests at the First Level of Reading: Elementary Reading
title: Recall stated facts
action: Recall a specific fact given in the passage, such as who designed an education or at what age something happened.
check: Can I point to the sentence that gives this fact?

subtopic: I. Exercises and Tests at the First Level of Reading: Elementary Reading
title: Notice exact wording
action: Distinguish between options that differ only in whether the text's own quoted wording is used.
check: Did I notice that the text put this word in quotation marks?

subtopic: I. Exercises and Tests at the First Level of Reading: Elementary Reading
title: Several answers may be correct
action: Identify all options that fit, such as authors who probably influenced the subject.
check: Have I checked every option rather than stopping at the first?

subtopic: I. Exercises and Tests at the First Level of Reading: Elementary Reading
title: What is not in the text
action: Identify which of several items is not mentioned in the passage.
check: Can I confirm each other item actually appears in the text?

subtopic: I. Exercises and Tests at the First Level of Reading: Elementary Reading
title: Likely or not likely today
action: Judge whether the subject, were he alive today, would likely hold each listed position, given his views.
check: Do my judgments follow from what the text says he believed?

subtopic: I. Exercises and Tests at the First Level of Reading: Elementary Reading
title: Infer an attitude
action: Infer from the text how the subject regarded a person, choosing all fitting descriptions.
check: Which sentences support the inference I drew?

subtopic: I. Exercises and Tests at the First Level of Reading: Elementary Reading
title: True or false detail
action: Decide whether a plausible-sounding statement about the subject's life is true or false according to the text.
check: Does the text support or contradict every part of the statement?

subtopic: I. Exercises and Tests at the First Level of Reading: Elementary Reading
title: Define a field of study
action: Choose the correct general definition of a field named in the text, using background knowledge.
check: Is my definition the general one, not a narrower part of it?

subtopic: I. Exercises and Tests at the First Level of Reading: Elementary Reading
title: What the work explained
action: Identify what a work described in the passage actually explained, distinguishing how something happens from why.
check: Does the work explain how, or why, it operates?

subtopic: I. Exercises and Tests at the First Level of Reading: Elementary Reading
title: Comment on a quotation
action: Comment in about 250 words on a memorable statement quoted in the text, including its metaphor.
check: Did I discuss the metaphor as well as the obvious point?

subtopic: I. Exercises and Tests at the First Level of Reading: Elementary Reading
title: Bring what you know
action: Bring relevant information you already have to bear on whatever you read; the better informed, the better you read.
check: Did I use my background knowledge to understand the text?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Two steps of inspection
action: Do inspectional reading in two steps: first pre-reading or skimming, then superficial reading.
check: Did I skim first and read superficially second?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Treat contents as a book
action: Treat a table of contents as though it were a book in itself and inspect it systematically.
check: Did I read the contents for the structure of the whole work?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Read author note first
action: Before skimming, read the author's biographical note in a few minutes to see what the author is planning and doing.
check: Do I know enough about the author to grasp his plan?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Skim in ten minutes
action: Spend less than ten minutes systematically skimming the whole table of contents; here speed is of the essence.
check: Did I finish skimming within ten minutes?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Count major parts
action: State how many major parts the work is divided into and what they are titled.
check: Can I name every major part?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Identify subdivisions
action: State what the major parts are subdivided into, how many there are, and whether they are equal.
check: Did I count the subdivisions in each part?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Principle of division
action: Say on what principle each major part seems to be divided.
check: What ordering principle do the headings follow?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Direction of movement
action: Say in which direction the action moves within each major part.
check: Do the headings show movement downwards or upwards?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Locate an episode
action: Say in which major part of the work a named episode occurs.
check: Can I find the heading where it appears?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Read superficially
action: After skimming and answering, take about twenty minutes to read the table of contents superficially.
check: Did I read straight through without stopping over difficulties?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Who guides whom
action: Identify key figures and their roles, such as who guides the protagonist and who sent the guide.
check: Can I state each figure's role from the contents?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Author's main concern
action: Say what the author's main concern is in the work.
check: Is my answer the concern of the whole work?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: What kind of work
action: Classify what kind of work it is, choosing all fitting descriptions.
check: Have I avoided being misled by the title?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Most influential tradition
action: Judge which ideology or teaching the work seems most dependent on.
check: Which tradition do the contents most reflect?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Significance of a symbol
action: Explain the significance of a symbolic detail or event mentioned in the contents.
check: What second meaning does this detail carry?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Why does this happen
action: Explain why a structural event occurs, such as why the travellers reach a particular place or why a guide departs.
check: Can I give a reason consistent with the work's scheme?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Guess without outside help
action: Try to answer the hard symbolism questions from the contents alone, then see how close your guesses are.
check: How close were my unaided guesses?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Read bio, then skim
action: Read the author's biography quickly, in five or six minutes, then pre-read the contents in no more than ten.
check: Did I keep within the time limits?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: What the book covers
action: Decide true or false whether the book undertakes a given subject, judging scope from the contents.
check: Do the chapter headings actually cover that subject?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Count the chapters
action: State how many chapters the work is divided into.
check: Did I count from the contents?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Does author face objections
action: Decide whether the author takes account of difficulties and objections against his theory.
check: Is there a chapter devoted to objections?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Is there a summing up
action: Decide whether the book has a chapter summing up its theory and conclusions.
check: Does the last chapter recapitulate?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Facts from author note
action: Answer questions about the author drawn from the biographical note, such as his habits or key life events.
check: Can I recall these details from the note?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Author's view of evidence
action: Say how the author regards a source of data he uses, e.g. complete or incomplete but invaluable.
check: Which heading reveals his assessment?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Define key terms
action: Define the key terms the book turns on, and how they relate to one another.
check: Can I state each term's meaning and its relation to the others?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Major or minor factors
action: Judge which factors play a major and which a minor role in the author's theory.
check: Do the contents give each factor a chapter or prominent place?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Which is greater
action: Say which of two things the author compares he thinks greater.
check: Which heading states the comparison?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Translate and interpret phrase
action: Translate a key phrase appearing in the contents and state its significance for the author's theory.
check: Is the sense clear from the contents even without translation?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Significance of a factor
action: Explain the significance of a factor the contents name for the author's subject.
check: Can I tie this factor to the main theory?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: State the problem
action: State fairly exactly, in a sentence or two, the problem the work sets out to solve.
check: Is my statement exact and only a sentence or two?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Theory in a nutshell
action: State the author's theory in a nutshell, in no more than 100 words.
check: Is it under 100 words and does it cover the whole?

subtopic: II. Exercises and Tests at the Second Level of Reading: Inspectional Reading
title: Seek better answers
action: Let questions you could not answer lead you to search the works themselves for better answers.
check: Did I go to the work itself to settle what I could not answer?

subtopic: III. Exercises and Tests at the Third Level of Reading: Analytical Reading
title: Answer the four questions
action: Answer the four questions about this book: what it is about, what is said and how, is it true, what of it.
check: Can I answer all four questions about this book myself?

subtopic: III. Exercises and Tests at the Third Level of Reading: Analytical Reading
title: Be your own judge
action: Judge for yourself whether you have answered; no answers are given, they are in the book itself.
check: Can I find support for each answer in the book?

subtopic: III. Exercises and Tests at the Third Level of Reading: Analytical Reading
title: Work alone
action: Apply the rules to the given book yourself, relying on your own thought.
check: Did I rely on my own mind rather than outside help?

subtopic: III. Exercises and Tests at the Third Level of Reading: Analytical Reading
title: Classify this book
action: Apply the first rule of structural analysis: classify this book (it is a practical book).
check: Have I said what kind of book it is and why?

subtopic: III. Exercises and Tests at the Third Level of Reading: Analytical Reading
title: State unity briefly
action: State what the book is about as a whole more briefly than the authors do in any one place.
check: Is my statement shorter than any of the authors' own statements?

subtopic: III. Exercises and Tests at the Third Level of Reading: Analytical Reading
title: Outline and explain proportions
action: Outline the book's four parts and twenty-one chapters, and explain why each level of reading gets the space it does.
check: Can I say why elementary reading is short and analytical reading long?

subtopic: III. Exercises and Tests at the Third Level of Reading: Analytical Reading
title: Define the problem precisely
action: Define the problem the book sets out to solve with precision; it is not simply teaching you to read.
check: Did I describe the particular way and goals of reading, precisely?

subtopic: III. Exercises and Tests at the Third Level of Reading: Analytical Reading
title: Come to terms
action: Find the book's terms: the important words you and the authors must understand in common.
check: Have I listed the key words and their shared meanings?

subtopic: III. Exercises and Tests at the Third Level of Reading: Analytical Reading
title: State propositions
action: State the propositions the authors asserted, in your own words.
check: Can I restate each key proposition without the authors' wording?

subtopic: III. Exercises and Tests at the Third Level of Reading: Analytical Reading
title: Construct the arguments
action: Construct the book's arguments yourself, without the authors' help.
check: Can I lay out the reasoning behind the main claims?

subtopic: III. Exercises and Tests at the Third Level of Reading: Analytical Reading
title: Solved and unsolved problems
action: Determine which problems the book solved and which it did not, such as those involving individual differences.
check: Can I name a problem the book admits it did not solve?

subtopic: III. Exercises and Tests at the Third Level of Reading: Analytical Reading
title: Apply intellectual etiquette
action: Before criticising, apply the three general maxims of intellectual etiquette discussed in Chapter 10.
check: Have I understood before judging, and disagreed without contentiousness?

subtopic: III. Exercises and Tests at the Third Level of Reading: Analytical Reading
title: Apply the first three criteria
action: Apply the first three points of criticism yourself; the authors offer nothing on them.
check: Have I judged where, if anywhere, the book is uninformed, misinformed or illogical?

subtopic: III. Exercises and Tests at the Third Level of Reading: Analytical Reading
title: Show incompleteness
action: Show wherein the book's analysis is incomplete, starting from the authors' own admissions about elementary and syntopical reading.
check: Can I name a respect in which the analysis is incomplete?

subtopic: III. Exercises and Tests at the Third Level of Reading: Analytical Reading
title: First vs second intention
action: Ask whether the book distinguishes enough between reading a text and reading a commentary on it.
check: Does the book treat commentary-reading separately enough?

subtopic: III. Exercises and Tests at the Third Level of Reading: Analytical Reading
title: Heretical vs canonical texts
action: Ask whether enough is said about reading heretical versus canonical texts, and texts detached from both.
check: Is this distinction treated adequately?

subtopic: III. Exercises and Tests at the Third Level of Reading: Analytical Reading
title: Special vocabularies
action: Ask whether enough attention is paid to special vocabularies, especially in science and mathematics, and to lyric poetry.
check: Are special vocabularies and lyric poetry covered enough?

subtopic: III. Exercises and Tests at the Third Level of Reading: Analytical Reading
title: Find defects authors miss
action: Look for defects or failures in the book that are obvious to you though not to the authors.
check: Have I found any omission the authors did not admit?

subtopic: IV. Exercises and Tests at the Fourth Level of Reading: Syntopical Reading
title: Fix subject and texts
action: Take the preparatory step: decide the subject you wish to consider and the texts you will read.
check: Have I defined the subject and chosen the texts?

subtopic: IV. Exercises and Tests at the Fourth Level of Reading: Syntopical Reading
title: Narrow to one question
action: Narrow the inquiry to a single question that the texts can answer, framed as alternatives.
check: Is my question single and stated so each author can answer it?

subtopic: IV. Exercises and Tests at the Fourth Level of Reading: Syntopical Reading
title: Read carefully, no hurry
action: Read the texts carefully, taking as much time as needed, marking passages and returning as often as you wish.
check: Did I go back to the texts while answering?

subtopic: IV. Exercises and Tests at the Fourth Level of Reading: Syntopical Reading
title: Identify author's categories
action: Identify the distinct types or categories an author names in the text.
check: Can I list each category in the author's terms?

subtopic: IV. Exercises and Tests at the Fourth Level of Reading: Syntopical Reading
title: Common and different
action: State what the categories have in common and how they differ.
check: Have I stated both the shared features and the differences?

subtopic: IV. Exercises and Tests at the Fourth Level of Reading: Syntopical Reading
title: Order on a scale
action: Order the categories on a scale, such as from less to more inclusive.
check: Does my ordering follow the text's description?

subtopic: IV. Exercises and Tests at the Fourth Level of Reading: Syntopical Reading
title: Difference of degree or kind
action: Ask whether the good one category achieves is the same good in higher degree or a different good altogether.
check: Have I decided between degree and kind from the text?

subtopic: IV. Exercises and Tests at the Fourth Level of Reading: Syntopical Reading
title: Same in the same way?
action: Ask whether things that share a quality share it in the same way.
check: Did I distinguish the senses in which each has the quality?

subtopic: IV. Exercises and Tests at the Fourth Level of Reading: Syntopical Reading
title: Weigh a troubling remark
action: Notice a remark of the author's that raises a difficulty for your interpretation and ask what it implies.
check: Does this remark fit my reading or challenge it?

subtopic: IV. Exercises and Tests at the Fourth Level of Reading: Syntopical Reading
title: Author's main problem
action: State the main problem the second author poses about the subject.
check: Have I stated the problem in neutral terms both authors could address?

subtopic: IV. Exercises and Tests at the Fourth Level of Reading: Syntopical Reading
title: Same problem elsewhere?
action: Ask whether the author poses the same problem about a related subject.
check: Does the author treat the related case differently?

subtopic: IV. Exercises and Tests at the Fourth Level of Reading: Syntopical Reading
title: Opposite of key term
action: Identify what an author takes to be the opposite of a key term.
check: What does the author contrast this term with?

subtopic: IV. Exercises and Tests at the Fourth Level of Reading: Syntopical Reading
title: Basis of legitimacy
action: Identify what, for the author, makes the subject legitimate.
check: Can I name the author's basis in his own terms?

subtopic: IV. Exercises and Tests at the Fourth Level of Reading: Syntopical Reading
title: Test your interpretation
action: Having found the authors apparently disagreeing, consider whether that interpretation is correct and what in the texts casts doubt on it.
check: Is there anything either author says that undermines my interpretation?

subtopic: IV. Exercises and Tests at the Fourth Level of Reading: Syntopical Reading
title: Both, not either
action: Ask whether the author holds that the subject is both of the supposed alternatives.
check: Did I check for a 'both' answer before choosing one side?

subtopic: IV. Exercises and Tests at the Fourth Level of Reading: Syntopical Reading
title: Does the other agree
action: Ask whether the other author agrees with that position.
check: Have I checked the second author on the same point?

subtopic: IV. Exercises and Tests at the Fourth Level of Reading: Syntopical Reading
title: Extend the agreement
action: Ask whether the basic agreement between the authors extends to further points.
check: What further point do both share, and what key word names it?

subtopic: IV. Exercises and Tests at the Fourth Level of Reading: Syntopical Reading
title: Same word, same meaning?
action: Ask whether a shared key word means the same thing for both authors.
check: Does each author mean the same thing by this word?

subtopic: IV. Exercises and Tests at the Fourth Level of Reading: Syntopical Reading
title: Agreement on all points?
action: Ask whether agreement on the primary question means the texts agree on all points.
check: Have I noted points each raises that the other ignores?

subtopic: IV. Exercises and Tests at the Fourth Level of Reading: Syntopical Reading
title: Draw justified conclusions
action: Draw the conclusions about the subject that can justifiably be drawn from careful reading of the texts.
check: Does each conclusion follow from the texts read?

subtopic: IV. Exercises and Tests at the Fourth Level of Reading: Syntopical Reading
title: Document from the texts
action: Document your answers and conclusions from the authors' own texts, finding the passages that support each.
check: Can I cite the passage behind each answer?

subtopic: IV. Exercises and Tests at the Fourth Level of Reading: Syntopical Reading
title: Document disagreement
action: If you disagree with an answer or conclusion, document your disagreement with the authors' own words.
check: Have I backed my disagreement with quotations from the authors?
